:::{#exm-conditional-mean-precision}
#### The conditional mean and variance of the middle element of a chain of three Gaussian variables

<!-- no-figure: arithmetic on one 3 x 3 matrix; nothing to plot -->

Let $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2, X_3)}$ be the [Gaussian](#def-normal) vector of @exm-precision-zero-cind,
with $\E{\vX} = \matr{0}$ and

$$
\precision(\vX) = \pmat{2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2}.
$$

By @thm-conditional-mean-precision with $i = 2$,
using the second row of $\precision(\vX)$,

$$
\condE{X_2}{X_1 = x_1, X_3 = x_3}
= -\frac{-1}{2}x_1 - \frac{-1}{2}x_3
= \frac{x_1 + x_3}{2},
$$

and $\condVar{X_2}{X_1 = x_1, X_3 = x_3} = 1 / 2$.
So the best prediction of $X_2$ from its two neighbors is their average,
and it does not depend on anything else.
The first element has weight $-\precision(\vX)_{21} / \precision(\vX)_{22} = 1/2$,
and the weights would be zero for a neighbor with a zero precision-matrix element,
as @thm-precision-zero-cind says.

:::
